insight: The map shows how each Philippine province scores for solar potential on a 0‑100 scale. The average score is about 80, and the highest observed score is 87.33 in Davao del Sur, while the lowest is 68.73 in Cagayan. Scores are mainly driven by how much sunlight reaches the ground (solar irradiance) and how often the sky stays clear (high solar GHI). These factors directly affect how much electricity a solar panel can produce each year. Proximity to volcanoes or the sea does not change the score; the data shows zero volcanoes and no power plants influencing the map. Even provinces that are near volcanoes or on the coast can have only moderate scores if they have more cloud cover, terrain that blocks the sun, or lower irradiance values. For example, Cagayan records an irradiance of 3.62 kWh/m²/day and a moderate score of 68.73, while Davao del Sur enjoys 4.49 kWh/m²/day and a very high score of 87.33. This explains why clear‑sky conditions matter most for your roof’s solar savings.
